title: Add canonical model-ref test fixtures so invented refs cannot silently pass
goal: PROBLEM: Model references have a subtle grammar (shared/modelKeys.js: bare id, legacy provider::id, canonical harness::provider::id, and harness::provider::id::level; splitReasoning returns a reasoning level ONLY for 4-segment refs, so a 3-segment ref like google::m1::high parses as harness/provider/id with NO reasoning). An agent writing the AliasTargetChip reasoning-suffix test invented the 3-segment form expecting a ::high suffix; the test passed for the wrong reason (via the chip's sr-only full ref, not the muted-suffix span) and the silently-wrong coverage survived until a reviewer spotted it, costing a second fix-and-re-review commit. There is no canonical fixture module for model refs, so every agent invents refs from memory and can fall into the same trap. FIX: Add a canonical model-ref fixture module (follow the existing shared/toolLogFormat.fixtures.js pattern) exporting named valid refs for each grammar form plus documented INVALID traps (3-segment ::suffix is not reasoning; 5+ segments malformed), with a JSDoc table of form -> example -> parse result; link it from splitReasoning/parseModelKey JSDoc; migrate the alias chip/summary tests onto the fixtures; add one negative test asserting the 3-segment trap yields reasoning null. Case study: task 158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972 (docs/tasks/158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972/review-alias-redo-20261120.md non-blocking nit; fixed in the full-width follow-up per review-fullwidth-20261120.md).
